config.name: send_pc
config.notes: C3 repair r2 (orchestrator; user approved training on an AWS GPU, evaluation stays on the local CPU): train.steps 5000 -> 10000 for localisation accuracy (C2's 2500 steps / ~27 epochs left mm-level errors), and n_action_steps 4 -> 2 so the policy re-observes every 2 control steps, reducing open-loop drift near the hole mouth (predict() now returns (2, 9)). Point count follows the data (256 -> 512 points); the encoder takes any N. Run: python -m policy.train --config configs/send_pc.json --device cuda (env: policy/requirements-train-gpu.txt). C3 repair r1 (orchestrator, after the user moved the RGB-only baseline out of the send line): relative_pos = true (point cloud xyz, agent_pos positions and position actions relative to the last observed pin tip; rotations absolute; predict() still returns absolute poses) and train.steps 2500 -> 5000 (superseded by r2). The timing block below is the B5 measurement that set the earlier 2500. When the f5 RGB comparison is run (interview-evidence phase), configs/send_rgb.json must use the same train.steps and relative_pos as this file. f5 setup: the RGB branch uses Diffusion Policy's standard augmentation (random crop 96->88 per image in training, centre crop 88 at inference); the point cloud branch has no augmentation. Everything else (demos, diffusion head, pose + wrench conditioning, train section incl. steps) is identical in both configs. B5 timing was measured before the crop was added (96x96 input), so the RGB estimate is conservative.

timing.note: measured while the simulator agent ran; re-measure when idle
